# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: LORD STRANLEIGH ABROAD (Robert Barr, 1913; Ward, Lock & Co.; Gutenberg 32185)

Contents: I Lord Stranleigh All at Sea (p7); II An Automobile Ride (49); III The God in the Car (87); IV The Mad Miss Maturin (125); V In Search of Game (164); VI The Bunk House Prisoner (209); VII The End of the Contest (259). Frontispiece: "'Why did you wish to murder me?'" (p189).

**Cast:** Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood (aliases: Edmund/Evelyn Trevelyan, Henry Johnson, "Edmund Stranleigh"; shy, rich, dislikes publicity, careless of money, claims wealth comes from "flukes"). Ponderby (valet, expressionless Londoner, dislikes America, "born a servant", blushes). Hon. John "Jack" Hazel (ex-Camperdown Club cardsharp, expelled; steerage ticket under name William Jones; later poker sting). Ship's doctor (friendly, Stranleigh's lunch neighbour). Purser (unnamed). Girl passenger (distant Trevelyan of Wychwood; purse stolen; Stranleigh lends £100). Charles Branksome/Branksome Poole (ruddy, thick-necked, blackmailer, ex-chauffeur, bigamous husband). His wife (dark head, unnamed; daughter of wealthy English father, eloped on 1909-ish motor tour in America; father disowned her, died 2 years later). Erasmus Blank (millionaire blackmail target). Wentworth Parkes (ex-valet of Duke of Rattleborough; forged letter; fraud). Duke of Rattleborough (cables Parkes = valet, bolted, "police yearning"). J.E. Sterling (young Detroit engineer, ~25; Woodbridge Street shop; safety-peg device). Sterling's middle-aged assistant. Challis: James "Jim" Challis (engineer, Fulmer's grist mill, Altonville). Gertrude Challis (née Anson). Stanmore Anson (old yeoman, Swedish ancestry, Anson's Mill, bankrupt). Mrs Anson (kindly). Asa Perkins (Boston; house Stranleigh rents). Edward "Ned" Trenton (Philadelphia coal/railway magnate). Mrs Vanderveldt (Trenton's sister; husband ex-Minister to Italy). Constance Maturin (friend; Powerville dams; mad-seeming conservationist). John L. Boscombe (reputed millionaire, Powerville control). John L. Banks (Ice Trust attorney). Stanley Armstrong (rancher; mining engineer; ex-Chicago). Mrs Armstrong. Professor Armstrong ("Miss Armstrong", doctor, Lausanne, Thun; "American Madame Curie"). Jim Dean (leader of six bunk-house men; ear shot). Silas A. Ricketts (Bleachers lawyer, $5000 note). Sheriff (Bleachers). Telegraph operator (Western Telegraph). Detective Burns (NY). Peter (ranch hand).

**Ch I (Southampton → Queenstown → NY):** Stranleigh boards largest liner, sails noon for Cherbourg. Meets doctor; asks him not to reveal "Evelyn Trevelyan = Lord Stranleigh". Meets Hazel (shabby, haggard), who insists on steerage. Stranleigh gets cabin 4390 from purser (name on steerage ticket William Jones; £5 notes; "one silly bet"). Hazel's name kept (Stranleigh: "your own colours"); promises no cards. Poker/card-sharp backstory. Girl at purser's window; Stranleigh gives her £100 (two £50 notes), Bank of England. Branksome Poole enters Stranleigh's suite demanding money for "wife" (two £50 notes, numbers read). Stranleigh refuses; Ponderby throws Poole out (first disobedience). Wife in Ponderby's room, tells story (eloped; husband forced her to hand him the notes; plan: detention in NY). Stranleigh arranges detention by wireless. Hazel poker game on deck: Poole deals, Hazel exposes cheating; chief officer, captain; Poole arrested; wireless: Charles Branksome wanted for blackmailing Erasmus Blank. Wife unmolested; has notes.

**Ch II (NY → Detroit):** Stranleigh changes hotels thrice with new names; newspapers pursue him. Parkes: letter from Duke of Rattleborough; Sterling Motor Co. option; $100,000 share; Parkes's glib pitch fails. Drive in Detroit car (Parkes drives). Cable to Rattleborough: "Letter a forgery… RATTLEBOROUGH." Stranleigh sails via Boston → St John NB → Canada → Detroit (Panama Canal not yet open). Ponderby pines for London. Hotel suite as "Henry Johnson". Chauffeur hired; Woodbridge Street, sign "J. E. STERLING. Motor Engineer. Repairs promptly executed. Satisfaction guaranteed." Shop: runabout in window; Sterling and assistant. Safety device under leather curtain: three pegs — centre stops engine & brakes; right peg turns right; left peg turns left. Stranleigh gets option for a week: $500 deposit (five $100 bills). Earlier Englishman had borrowed car, vanished. Parkes watches through window. Parkes-as-chauffeur drive to Lake St Clair (Canadian shore): Parkes demands $100,000 or dash car over bank; Stranleigh wrestles, uses pegs, stops car at edge; throws Parkes into shallow water. Stranleigh tells Parkes police want him; orders Parkes to sign no-molestation pledge; pay Parkes $500 + $500. Stranleigh: will capitalise company $100k–$500k.

**Ch III (Altonville, the Challises, Anson's mill):** Stranleigh and Ponderby reverse roles (Ponderby = "country gentleman", Stranleigh = chauffeur Henry Johnson). Burford/Lenthall/butler parable (£3000 story); Ponderby given $15,000 in Altonville bank. Drive north to lakes (mills, Trusts). Young couple on knoll; wife sprained ankle; Challis gives $1 tip; doctor (in Altonville) treats her. Challis is engineer (technical college; firm Langdon, Bliss & Co.; reports on mills). Visited Anson's mill (old overshot waterwheels). Anson raged at Langdon; Challis's report leaked; dismissed. Challis married Gertrude Anson (she chose to; father disowned). Gertrude refuses drive. Anson's mill auction Nov 17 (posters). Anson house also for sale. Stranleigh visits Mrs Anson (asks wardrobe for Gertrude); Mr Perkins's storeroom. Stanmore Anson interview: "connected with G.K.R. Trust?" "Not unless compelled by force of law." Stranleigh pays Anson's figure for mill + ten acres; Anson demands manager; Challis as manager; Anson reconciles. Gertrude: "Father, Jim says he's going to scrap all the machinery… Shall we throw our differences on that scrap-heap?"

**Ch IV (Trenton's Pennsylvania estate; Powerville):** Ned Trenton, Philadelphia-based; father left estate to Trenton and sister; Sis = Mrs Vanderveldt. Constance Maturin (father's Powerville company, minority stock; Boscombe controls). Trenton's conservation lawsuit; Maturin's dam (father's) vs Trenton's dam; Trenton blew up his dam with dynamite. Lakes with telephone-linked caretakers; "Vallombrosa". Mrs Vanderveldt: Maturin travelled to England to meet Stranleigh to seek capitalist. Maturin's six-cylinder runabout; Stranleigh offers money; "You're a very persistent person." Stranleigh: "I am that capitalist." Maturin admits model city on heights above Powerville; banks withdraw. Stranleigh's brokers fail to buy stock. Boscombe warns Stranleigh: "stark mad" woman. Festival: entertainment for valley workers; dam bursts (sluice wave); town and mills destroyed. Boscombe: "This is murder!" Stranleigh: "Whoever is responsible… should be hanged!"

**Ch V (University Club; Armstrong ranch, shot):** Stranleigh in NY (University Club, July heat). Banks (Ice Trust) advises ranch cure; gives letter to Stanley Armstrong. Stranleigh hires guide, horses, mules at Bleachers station (paid in advance). Clearing near ranch: shot in left shoulder (Jim Dean). Guide and escort abandon; packs dumped. Stranleigh raises arms, shouts parley. Reaches house; Mrs Armstrong, then Miss Armstrong (doctor; dresses shoulder, sling). Armstrong in Chicago. Verandah talk: Thun, Falken inn, Lausanne, cookery school. Jim Dean (whistle; "wanted to nip you"; mistaken for sheriff). Stranleigh's cigarettes; Miss Armstrong's debts: Ricketts holds $5000 note on ranch; silver mine. Stranleigh offers to lend $3000 (she has $2000); Miss Armstrong accepts as "business".

**Ch VI (bunk house; Ricketts; telegrams):** Ranch: bunk house (stone, 12 bunks), cooking shack, mine 500 yards south, cascade 100 ft. Stranleigh explores mine; Jim's men warn; rock returned into mine (dynamite stored). Stranleigh rides to Bleachers (trailed by Jim); visits Ricketts ($5/hour; "Armstrong's letter from Chicago"). Telegraph operator; Stranleigh sends wire to NY detective and $20,000 express order; another wire to Pinkerton Chicago offering $100 (decoy; Ricketts bribed operator $1). Stranleigh captured at dusk by six men; held in bunk house; supper; cigars; Jim's "cohoots" accusation; Stranleigh's "brain vs muscle" talk; Jim demands he lend Armstrong money ($ for mine); Stranleigh refuses; "rank brigandage". Stranleigh guard-prisoner; nights of talk; he suggests waterwheel on falls.

**Ch VII (escape; sale; deed):** Stranleigh climbs chimney (soot), goes to house, takes magazine rifle, bread, ham, tobacco, candles, bedding; builds rock wall across mine mouth, interstices dynamite. Dawn: shoots Jim's left ear (sentinel); Jim's door punctured with letter "S". Parley: "Hague tribunal"; threat to blow mine; armistice. Jim's ear bandaged with fine embroidered handkerchief (crest & monogram); Miss Armstrong deduces the shooter was above, not Jim's gun. Stranleigh rides out, meets Armstrong on road (Armstrong borrowed $500 from Stranleigh, to bribe sheriff). Auction at Agricultural Hall: Ricketts bids $3000; Stranleigh $5000; bids escalate; Ricketts $16,000; Stranleigh $17,000 (cash, counted $17,000 on sheriff's table). Stranleigh gives Miss Armstrong envelope with deed as "payment of medical bill" (and Jim's bill). Conditions: keep ranch in her name; Armstrong gets ~$10–12k; she to develop mine; Banks to forward news. Miss Armstrong: "Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood" — she knew from NY paper and handkerchief crest. THE END.

Other Book 1 details: "Lord Stranleigh" ~ Ponderby's 37 suits; Hazel's Camperdown Club; Ponderby "my lord" vs "Henry" disguise; Sterling's option, deposit "five hundred"; Stranleigh's "pistol in Texas" (automatic pistol).

---

## BOOK 2: THE POMP OF YESTERDAY (Joseph Hocking; Hodder & Stoughton; Gutenberg 25136)

Epigraph: Kipling "Recessional" stanza. Foreword (author, March 1918): Victory "delayed"; story vs polemic; descriptions of Somme from witnesses; Author revisited Front; finished writing Aug 1917 (Russia prediction).

Narrator: Captain Luscombe (Cornish, recruiter, then battalion officer; Edgecumbe's friend; ~39; "over six feet", ~12 stone). Chapters I–XLII (titles as in contents).

**Ch I (Plymouth, spring 1915):** Narrator at Plymouth harbour meets man from Bombay, unknown, lost memory; motley clothes, L5 notes in vest; name chosen "Paul Edgecumbe" (after Mount Edgecumbe; "Paul" scriptural). Hotel on The Hoe; Luscombe pays. Recruiting meeting; Edgecumbe volunteers: "Will you take me, sir?… how can a man, who is a man, do anything else?" Other volunteers follow. Edgecumbe: scars from Indians; saluted soldiers.

**Ch II (Sir Roger Granville):** Luscombe telegraphed to Falmouth; Edgecumbe lost. Colonel Gray (Exeter); Sir Roger Granville (meeting chairman; Granitelands; Devonshire). George St Mabyn (captain, Territorials, Ypres, wounded; engaged to Norah Blackwater). Maurice St Mabyn (elder brother, killed in Egypt; fiancé was Norah).

**Ch III (St Mabyn's behaviour):** Norah Blackwater (~25, tall, furtive, cold). Lorna Bolivick (~19–20, brown eyes, childlike, "Lorna Doone" joke; father Sir Thomas, two brothers; home Bolivick near South Petherwin). Luscombe suspects Edgecumbe = Maurice; St Mabyn's ashen face. Lorna makes Luscombe promise to find Edgecumbe "as if he were your own brother". St Mabyn invites Luscombe to lunch at his house (Elizabethan, lichen walls, deer park).

**Ch IV (Springfield):** Captain Horace Springfield (30–35, tall, dark, thin, receding forehead, greying black hair, deep eyes, scar on cheek below right temple). Maurice died in Egypt (mullah rebellion) with Springfield present. Lorna gets diary promise, May 29: Luscombe to write her on finding Edgecumbe; she witnesses ("Witnessed by Lorna Bolivick, Bolivick, South Petherwin"). Norah: Springfield "snakes". Luscombe at front winter 1915–16; captured in raid, cave with German officer.

**Ch V (Miracle):** Sergeant Smith; bombardment; Edgecumbe (English voice, German-speaking) persuades ~30 Germans to surrender; footnote says incident real (told by British officer).

**Ch VI (Memory):** Edgecumbe reunited; Luscombe's colonel (unnamed) decorates; Edgecumbe missing. Luscombe tests memory: Devonshire, Granitelands, Maurice St Mabyn, Norah Blackwater, Springfield (Edgecumbe says "I don't think I like him").

**Ch VII (Drink):** Edgecumbe wounded; "I have no name" monologue on drink: ships held in Plymouth harbour (firemen drunk); munitions workers absent; 10% munition loss; grain for brewing; King, Kitchener, Chancellor pledged. Major St Mabyn enters; sees Edgecumbe; asks "What did you say your name was?" "D.C.L.I."

**Ch VIII (Eavesdropper):** St Mabyn: engaged to Norah (announced). Luscombe overhears in copse near St Pinto: Springfield & St Mabyn — "if it is he, he must never go back to England alive"; "Are you sure Luscombe has no suspicions?"; Springfield: "Foul play… too deep in this business". St Mabyn's note invites Luscombe Thursday.

**Ch IX (Missing):** Luscombe's dinner with Springfield and St Mabyn; Springfield probes. Edgecumbe leaves billet at midnight; two minutes later angry voices, pistol shot. Edgecumbe missing.

**Ch X (Somme, July 1916):** Lorna letter (poor Tommy legless; asks for photograph; "I command you"). Luscombe sends Edgecumbe's photograph. Somme attack; Luscombe captured/beaten by three Germans; Edgecumbe rescues him: "I have found more than life."

**Ch XI (Y.M.C.A.):** Edgecumbe converted at Y.M.C.A. hut (heard Gospel, New Testament). Springfield makes Indian cry; Edgecumbe: "I know that voice." Lorna's letter: photograph "strange-looking man… wonderful eyes". Luscombe concludes Edgecumbe ≠ Maurice; Springfield and St Mabyn involved.

**Ch XII (Somme, July):** Shelling; Edgecumbe digs out Springfield under debris; Luscombe shell-shocked; doctor says Luscombe claims no rescue. Springfield "very bad". Colonel Gray: Edgecumbe to be decorated.

**Ch XIII (Madness):** Edgecumbe on boat home: Christianity; "Sermon on the Mount"; "war in the wrong way"; "we have forgotten God"; Sir William Robertson ("Make the men religious, Bishop"); Admiral Beatty's letter; Victor Hugo (Waterloo, God against Napoleon).

**Ch XIV (Logic):** Drink and impurity; Edgecumbe's argument; Luscombe's invitation from Lorna ("I shall take no refusal"); Edgecumbe agrees to go.

**Ch XV (Devonshire):** Colonel Heywood (OTC): Edgecumbe is an artillery officer, gunnery genius. Train to South Petherwin; carriage; Bolivick; Edgecumbe: "Must not God be beautiful?"

**Ch XVI (Bolivick):** Edgecumbe stares at Lorna ("In my dreams"). Sir Thomas Bolivick; Norah Blackwater at dinner. Luscombe tells Thirty-Germans story; Sir Thomas honours Edgecumbe.

**Ch XVII (New Development):** Charlie Buller (24, Devonshire yeomanry lieutenant, wounded, suitor, weak leg). Springfield arrives with Buller. Springfield's shock at Edgecumbe's name; thanks him. Edgecumbe confesses love to Luscombe; claims Springfield is dangerous ("serpent").

**Ch XVIII (Tragic):** Edgecumbe: "I know him… that man knows me." Lorna says Edgecumbe avoids her; Luscombe defends. Edgecumbe collapses at dusk (before dinner), pale, dying.

**Ch XIX (Mysterious Illness):** Dr Merril (South Petherwin). Suspects poison. Luscombe asks Sir Thomas for car; Buller can't drive; Springfield offers to drive, Luscombe declines; Springfield drinks liqueur. Luscombe drives to Plymouth with Buller to fetch Colonel McClure (St George's Military Hospital; 12 years in India).

**Ch XX (Night):** McClure examines symptoms; drive back; Springfield left about midnight; Lorna still up; Buller says Springfield "heir to a peerage" (St Mabyn says). Sir Thomas: "It's all over."

**Ch XXI (McClure's Verdict):** Edgecumbe's hands; blue spot below elbow; McClure's injection of antidote; Edgecumbe revives. McClure believes poisoned by Indian method; "watch over him."

**Ch XXII (Resolve):** Edgecumbe vows to marry Lorna; Luscombe raises objections (poverty; Buller; Springfield; "you may have a wife"). Springfield and Buller come to lunch; Springfield with Lorna.

**Ch XXIII (Springfield's Progress):** Luscombe questions Springfield (India, poisoning, Indian injection-prick). Springfield unmoved. Sir Thomas favours Springfield (heir to Lord Carbis, brewer, peer since 1890, Carbis Castle). McClure: "your friend was poisoned." Edgecumbe says he'll ask Lorna.

**Ch XXIV (Love-Making):** Edgecumbe's proposal in woodland walk (autumn); Lorna refuses ("I don't love you"); he says she will; vows; Springfield's "serpent" warnings.

**Ch XXV (Why Is Victory Delayed?):** Train to London; Luscombe reads The Times; Edgecumbe: "Then where does God come in?" Kipling "Recessional" quoted; Germany "lesser breeds without the law". Edgecumbe plans to study London. Springfield at Paddington.

**Ch XXVI (Where Does God Come In?):** Springfield joins them, friendly, offers London tour. Edgecumbe on leave (ill). YMCA hut at Hotel. Edgecumbe with Springfield to clubs; House of Commons; Cabinet Minister (old golf friend of Luscombe): "Where does God come in?" Lloyd George 1915 quote on drink. Waterloo station.

**Ch XXVII (Seeing London):** Waterloo station welcomes soldiers; vice; music-hall revue (vulgar); tea hotel; night London; Piccadilly, Haymarket, Pall Mall.

**Ch XXVIII (Sunshine and Shadow):** Churches; Hyde Park; Crystal Palace (sailors); Sunday sermon "they that were ready went into the marriage feast". Restaurant: Sir Thomas, Lorna, Springfield together; Edgecumbe: "battle royal… to save a woman's soul."

**Ch XXIX (Cross Currents):** Springfield now Colonel (to battalion). Edgecumbe's anti-drink monologue; Russia; "Purge England of her sins". Springfield proposes to Lorna at Bolivick (dinner) — disputed. Edgecumbe ordered to front.

**Ch XXX (March of Events, 1917):** Letters from Edgecumbe (Vimy, Lens, Lille; German evacuation; unrestricted U-boat warfare Feb 1; food shortage; Russian Revolution; US declares war; Wilson "prophetic utterance"; Kaiser prediction). June 1917: Edgecumbe appears at training camp, arm in sling.

**Ch XXXI (Edgecumbe's Return):** Springfield and St Mabyn at Vimy Ridge/Ypres/Messines. Springfield framed Edgecumbe (poison/spy charge, "Berlin" German uniform); Edgecumbe's trick spiked it; DSO. The Times praises him. Luscombe given leave.

**Ch XXXII (The Great Meeting):** National Hotel, London; mass meeting on drink and impurity; Cabinet Minister and General speak; Edgecumbe rises ("My lord… May I say a few words?"); tremendous speech; old clergyman prays; General: "worth more… than an army corps."

**Ch XXXIII (Lifted Curtain):** Telegram from Bolivick ("Come at once and bring your friend"). Lord & Lady Carbis (50s) to dinner, surprise for Lorna. Edgecumbe sees Lord Carbis; Lady Carbis: "John!… it's Jack! our Jack!" Edgecumbe collapses/faints.

**Ch XXXIV (Memory):** Memory restored ("the mists, the cobwebs, the black curtain"). Lady Carbis: "Mother!" Jack Carbis, son of Lord Carbis. Dinner party reaction; Lady Bolivick; Springfield's views.

**Ch XXXV (Afterwards):** Carbis family's joy. Jack's fear of sleep. Dr Merril examines.

**Ch XXXVI (Resolution):** Jack's name "Jack Carbis"; Lorna's view ("Paul Edgecumbe nicer"); Jack refuses drink-money from father ("not benefit by it"). Lorna: "Springfield's power over me" (unexplained). Luscombe: Springfield still wants Lorna.

**Ch XXXVII (Maurice St Mabyn):** Jack tells story: Maurice alive; Bizna, July 1914; Springfield attacked Maurice in Egypt/India; Maurice reported to General Gregory; Maurice's servant; attacked on road, tortured by Turks; Maurice imprisoned; Jack/Maurice conversation.

**Ch XXXVIII (Bombshell):** Family dinner (Lord & Lady Carbis, Lady Bolivick, Sir Thomas, Lorna, Norah, George St Mabyn, Springfield). Jack accuses Springfield of murdering Maurice; Springfield denies; proposes to Lorna under threat of exposure.

**Ch XXXIX (Springfield at Bay):** Springfield's counter-attack; Maurice St Mabyn enters ("You thought I was dead, eh?"); Springfield tries to protest; Maurice's contempt; Lorna leaves silently; Springfield departs.

**Ch XL (Maurice's Generosity):** Maurice forgives George; Norah loves Maurice still (he refuses). Luscombe with Lorna in rosery: Lorna says she'll never marry Jack; Sir Thomas: Springfield found dead in Plymouth hotel, injected Indian poison; sealed letter.

**Ch XLI (New Hope):** Springfield's suicide letter ("Life's not worth living… the great secret… solve"). Sealed package not to be opened within a week of burial. August: Lorna's letter asks Luscombe to visit. Jack at Carbis home, sees Luscombe; "the mills of God grind slowly".

**Ch XLII (Unfinished Story):** Luscombe at Bolivick; Lorna admits Springfield blackmailed her with threats against Jack (in letter). Luscombe reveals Springfield's villainy. Jack appears (motored 150 miles); Jack and Lorna walk; engagement; Luscombe kissed by Lorna; Jack to "beard the lion" (Sir Thomas). Ends mid-story.
